name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment-2 (FLEX-2)
facility: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA)
lead_investigators: Forman A. Williams (UC San Diego, Principal Investigator)
Vedha Nayagam (NCSER / Case Western Reserve University)
Daniel L. Dietrich (NASA Glenn Research Center)
Michael C. Hicks (NASA Glenn Research Center)
description: FLEX-2 extended microgravity droplet combustion research to binary fuel mixtures (n-heptane with n-hexadecane, and ethanol-water mixtures) and detailed quantitative characterization of sustained low-temperature 'cool flame' burning. Following apparent radiative extinction of the visible hot flame, droplets were observed to continue evaporating and burning in a low-temperature regime governed by low-temperature hydrocarbon chemical kinetics without visible soot or chemiluminescence.
apparatus: Advanced MDCA droplet dispenser inside the CIR, featuring dual fiber-supported and free-floating droplet deployment, intensified camera arrays (ICCD) for OH* and CH* chemiluminescence, and wideband radiometers.
